subject.title: Feature: Pre-compaction agent notification, structured handoff window, and deferral mechanism

question: Should OpenClaw add a new core compaction lifecycle contract for configurable pre-threshold warnings, a structured handoff checkpoint, and bounded defer, or keep the current notifyUser/hooks/memoryFlush/checkpoint model?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the proposed solution adds public config/tool/protocol surface and security-sensitive authority continuity semantics across a compaction boundary.

options.title: Design Core Lifecycle Contract
options.body: Define the warning thresholds, checkpoint envelope, deferral outcomes, audit records, security limits, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep Current Primitives
options.body: Document the existing notifyUser, compaction hooks, memoryFlush, and branch/restore checkpoint APIs as the supported extension points and close or narrow this feature direction later.

options.title: Split Into Smaller Decisions
options.body: Track pre-threshold warnings, handoff checkpoint schema, and bounded deferral as separately approved design items to reduce surface risk.

recommendation.title: Design Core Lifecycle Contract
recommendation.body: Define the warning thresholds, checkpoint envelope, deferral outcomes, audit records, security limits, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history signal for memoryFlush/compaction product behavior and the unresolved choice is product and security direction.
